title: Flying over 1904 Prairie Avenue asks far less of a phone
items: From the air, a phone was drawing Prairie Avenue's houses as tens of thousands of small pieces, each sent to the graphics chip on its own: about 28,000 draws a frame at the height Read frame pacing flies. Pieces of a house that sit side by side now go as one, and the same view takes about 2,900.
The ground, the yards and the railway yard are sent the same way, in every year.
Nothing you can see changes: every triangle, colour and shadow is the one drawn before, and a phone still skips the parts of a house outside its view when you stand close.
